title: Rigveda 5.82: To Savitri
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.82: To Savitri: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.82 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Savitri. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 396r-397r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.82.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 396r
translation.original_text:
1tat sa̍vi̱tur vṛ̍ṇīmahe va̱yaṁ de̱vasya̱ bhoja̍nam | śreṣṭha̍ṁ sarva̱dhāta̍ma̱ṁ tura̱m bhaga̍sya dhīmahi ||
2asya̱ hi svaya̍śastaraṁ savi̱tuḥ kac ca̱na pri̱yam | na mi̱nanti̍ sva̱rājya̍m ||
translation.text:
1WE crave of Savitar the God this treasure much to be enjoyed. The best, all-yielding, conquering gift of Bhaga we would gladly win.
2Savitar's own supremacy, most glorious and beloved of all, No one diminisheth in aught.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 396r (numbered 69r by the scribe) (OPenn image 396, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.81.4 ‹-bhavasi deva dharma-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 396v (numbered 69v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.82.3 ‹-ratnāni dāśuṣe suvāti savitā›. Verses 5.82.1-2 end on this page.

2asya | hi | svayaśaḥ-taram | savituḥ | kat | cana | priyam | na | minanti | sva-rājyam

translation.original_ref: RV 5.82.3-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 396v
translation.original_text:
3sa hi ratnā̍ni dā̱śuṣe̍ su̱vāti̍ savi̱tā bhaga̍ḥ | tam bhā̱gaṁ ci̱tram ī̍mahe ||
4a̱dyā no̍ deva savitaḥ pra̱jāva̍t sāvī̱ḥ saubha̍gam | parā̍ du̱ṣṣvapnya̍ṁ suva ||
5viśvā̍ni deva savitar duri̱tāni̱ parā̍ suva | yad bha̱draṁ tan na̱ ā su̍va ||
6anā̍gaso̱ adi̍taye de̱vasya̍ savi̱tuḥ sa̱ve | viśvā̍ vā̱māni̍ dhīmahi ||
7ā vi̱śvade̍va̱ṁ satpa̍tiṁ sū̱ktair a̱dyā vṛ̍ṇīmahe | sa̱tyasa̍vaṁ savi̱tāra̍m ||
8ya i̱me u̱bhe aha̍nī pu̱ra ety apra̍yucchan | svā̱dhīr de̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā ||
translation.text:
3For Savitar who is Bhaga shall send riches to his worshipper. That wondrous portion we implore.
4Send us this day, God Savitar, prosperity with progeny. Drive thou the evil dream away.
5Savitar, God, send far away all sorrows and calamities, And send us only what is good.
6Sinless in sight of Aditi through the God Savitar's influence, May we obtain all lovely things.
7We with our hymns this day elect the general God, Lord of the good, Savitar whose decrees are true.
8He who for ever vigilant precedes these Twain, the Day and Night, Is Savitar the thoughtful God.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 396v (numbered 69v by the scribe) (OPenn image 397, upper leaf). The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 397r (numbered 70r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.82.9 ‹-suvāti savitā›. Verses 5.82.3-8 end on this page; 5.82.3 begins on fol. 396r (numbered 69r by the scribe).

4adya | naḥ | deva | savitariti | prajāvat | sāvīḥ | saubhagam | parā | duḥ-svapnyam | suva
5viśvāni | deva | savitaḥ | duḥ-itāni | parā | suva | yat | bhadram | tat | naḥ | ā | suva
6anāgasaḥ | aditaye | devasya | savituḥ | save | viśvā | vāmāni | dhīmahi

8yaḥ | ime iti | ubhe iti | ahanī iti | puraḥ | eti | apra-yucchan | su-ādhīḥ | devaḥ | savitā

translation.original_ref: RV 5.82.9 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 397r
translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>ya i̱mā viśvā̍ jā̱tāny ā̍śrā̱vaya̍ti̱ śloke̍na | pra ca̍ su̱vāti̍ savi̱tā ||
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>He who gives glory unto all these living creatures with the song, And brings them forth, is Savitar.
